name: wifite2 - Automated Wireless Auditing
description: wifite2 automates the full wireless attack workflow: puts the card in monitor mode, scans for APs, and runs the best attack per target - WPA handshake capture + crack, PMKID, WPS (Pixie-Dust and PIN brute), and WEP. It orchestrates aircrack-ng/hcxdumptool/reaver/bully/hashcat so you point it at targets and collect cracked keys.
notes:
=== RUN ===
  wifite                         # auto monitor mode + scan; Ctrl-C to pick targets

=== SCOPE / FILTER ===
  wifite -i <interface>
  wifite --essid '<ssid>'
  wifite -b <target>             # target a BSSID
  wifite --kill                  # kill interfering processes

=== ATTACK SELECTION ===
  wifite --wpa                   # only WPA handshake attacks
  wifite --pmkid                 # clientless PMKID only
  wifite --wps                   # WPS (pixie-dust + pin)
  wifite --dict <wordlist>       # wordlist for cracking

=== OUTPUT ===
  # handshakes saved to ./hs/ ; cracked keys printed + stored in cracked.json

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  aircrack-ng suite (manual)
  hcxdumptool + hashcat (PMKID)
  bettercap (wifi module)

examples.label: Target one BSSID with a wordlist

recommended.note: aircrack-ng suite for the manual equivalent.

defense.why_it_works: wifite chains known wireless weaknesses (offline-crackable PSK handshakes, insecure WPS PIN/Pixie-Dust, WEP) into an automated pipeline, so any network with a weak passphrase or WPS enabled is quickly compromised.
defense.prerequisites: A monitor-mode-capable adapter within range of the target networks.
defense.impact: Automated recovery of Wi-Fi keys across many nearby networks with minimal operator effort.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1040] WIDS alerts for deauth floods, WPS PIN brute-force attempts, and rogue/monitor adapters; repeated association failures and handshake captures.
defense.artifacts: Wireless controller logs (WPS lockouts, deauth storms), reassociation spikes, WIDS rogue-device alerts.
defense.prevention: Disable WPS entirely; use WPA3-SAE or long random WPA2 passphrases; enable 802.11w PMF; prefer WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise; deploy WIPS; retire WEP/WPA-TKIP.
